entry.title: Missing Profit Center in G/L Line Items for Year-End Closing/Opening Documents (Italian Localization
entry.content:
Hello SAP Experts,

We are facing an issue with the year-end closing/opening documents (Document Type CL) in the Italian localization on SAP S/4HANA.

When using the "Display Line Items in General Ledger" app (F2217) for balance sheet accounts, the Profit Center field is completely blank for these closing/opening postings.
However, if we check the "Trial Balance" app, the balances are correctly carried forward and the Profit Center is accurately populated (e.g., an account with a 168k balance correctly shows Profit Center 'GENER' at 31/12 and 01/01 in the Trial Balance).

We have already checked the physical accounting document (Doc. Type CL) and confirmed that the Profit Center is indeed missing from the generated line items, which explains why the F2217 app cannot display it. Since our regulatory reporting heavily relies on the Line Items app, this missing analytical dimension is a blocking issue for our business users.

My questions are:

Why does the standard Italian closing/opening program aggregate these balances without carrying over the Profit Center dimension to the physical document line items?

How can we fix or configure the system for the future so that year-end closing/opening documents inherit and display the correct Profit Center at the line item level?

Thank you in advance for your support.

entry.title: SAP TechEd 2026 Berlin: Key Innovations, AI Breakthroughs and What's New in the SAP Ecosystem
entry.content:
SAP TechEd 2026 brings a new wave of enterprise innovation, putting AI agents, Joule Work, intelligent automation and connected business data at the center of the Autonomous Enterprise vision.

SAP TechEd 2026, held in Berlin, highlights SAP's continued commitment to transforming how businesses operate through artificial intelligence, intelligent automation and next-generation enterprise solutions.

This year's announcements reflect a major shift in SAP's AI strategy: moving beyond AI-powered assistance toward autonomous enterprise operations, where AI agents can understand business objectives, coordinate workflows, interact with enterprise applications and execute complex tasks with appropriate governance.

From enhancements to Joule Work and Joule Studio to the introduction of SAP Business AI Platform capabilities, SAP Business Data Cloud innovations and new AI models, TechEd 2026 introduces several developments that will shape the future of enterprise technology.

Let's explore the key announcements and innovations from SAP TechEd 2026.

1. Joule Work: Moving Towards Autonomous Business Operations

One of the biggest highlights of SAP TechEd 2026 is the continued evolution of Joule Work, SAP's AI-powered user experience designed to simplify complex business operations.

Joule Work enables users to describe a business goal in natural language, while AI orchestrates the required agents, applications and data across SAP and non-SAP systems to accomplish the task.

Some of the key enhancements include:

  • Advanced agentic thinking: Improved reasoning, planning and execution capabilities for complex business workflows.
  • Enterprise governance: Built-in audit trails, role-based permissions and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
  • Expanded SAP Knowledge Graph integration: Better business context to help AI agents understand customer-specific processes and data.
  • Secure agent-to-agent interoperability: Improved connectivity between SAP Joule Agents and third-party AI agents through a secure gateway.

These developments represent an important step toward an enterprise environment where AI agents can collaborate and execute connected business processes securely.

2. Joule Studio: Simplifying Enterprise AI Agent Development

SAP is also expanding Joule Studio, making it easier for developers and business users to build, customize and manage AI agents.

With deeper integration into Joule Work, Joule Studio provides a shared environment for creating custom agents, extending existing Joule Agents and orchestrating workflows.

Key innovations include:

  • Intent-based development: Developers can describe business requirements, and Joule Studio helps identify relevant processes, APIs, data and authorizations.
  • AI agent extensions: Existing Joule Agents can be enhanced with additional instructions, APIs, MCP connections and workflow triggers.
  • n8n integration: Enables orchestration of complex workflows across SAP and non-SAP applications.
  • Agent lifecycle management: New capabilities for testing, evaluating, deploying and monitoring agents.
  • Developer flexibility: Business users can define requirements through the web experience, while developers can continue working through their preferred IDE and CLI tools.

SAP is also introducing pre-deployment testing and offline evaluations to help organizations validate agent behavior before production deployment.

The objective is to make enterprise AI development more accessible while maintaining the governance and security required for business-critical applications.

3. SAP Business AI Platform: Building the Foundation for Enterprise AI

The SAP Business AI Platform is a major part of SAP's Autonomous Enterprise strategy.

It brings together the capabilities required to build, contextualize, reason and govern enterprise AI solutions.

The platform focuses on combining business process knowledge, trusted enterprise data, AI models and governance capabilities to help organizations move beyond isolated AI pilots.

Key announcements include:

SAP Enterprise AI Gateway

A new centralized governance solution designed to manage AI interactions across enterprise environments.

It will provide:

  • Centralized authentication and authorization.
  • AI traffic routing and policy enforcement.
  • Monitoring and usage tracking.
  • Auditing and governance.
  • Secure connectivity across MCPs, APIs, AI agents and large language models.

Built on SAP Integration Suite, the solution aims to simplify the management of enterprise AI interactions.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

SAP AI Agent Hub

SAP is expanding AI agent governance capabilities to provide better visibility and control over SAP and third-party AI agents.

A new AI Governance Assistant will also help organizations assess AI systems against regulatory requirements, including the EU AI Act.

This will support risk classification, documentation reviews and ongoing compliance assessments.

4. SAP Business Data Cloud: Advancing Enterprise Data Management

Data remains one of the most important foundations for successful enterprise AI adoption.

At TechEd 2026, SAP announced new SAP Business Data Cloud capabilities designed to make enterprise data more accessible, reusable and valuable for AI and analytics.

Some major innovations include:

Expanded Lakehouse Capabilities

SAP is introducing native support for Apache Iceberg and a distributed SQL query engine, supported by Dremio technology.

These capabilities will help organizations access and process SAP and third-party data across hybrid and multi-cloud environments.

Potential benefits include:

  • Reduced data duplication.
  • Faster access to business insights.
  • Improved query performance.
  • Greater flexibility in data architecture.
  • Consistent governance across data environments.

SAP Business Data Cloud Ontology Manager

A new AI-assisted solution designed to help organizations create and manage domain-specific business ontologies.

It will enable businesses to organize relationships, rules and processes into reusable business context that AI agents can understand.

Enhanced SAP Knowledge Graph

SAP Knowledge Graph will gain support for additional SAP-managed and customer-managed data products.

This will help Joule and other AI agents understand company-specific business relationships and provide more relevant, context-aware responses.

Together, these innovations strengthen SAP's business data fabric strategy and provide a more reliable foundation for enterprise AI.

5. SAP HANA Cloud: AI-Powered Database Administration

SAP is bringing new agentic AI capabilities to SAP HANA Cloud to simplify database administration.

Database administrators will be able to use a conversational interface to perform tasks such as:

  • Monitoring database health.
  • Troubleshooting technical issues.
  • Optimizing SQL queries and database performance.
  • Managing database lifecycle operations.
  • Diagnosing and resolving operational issues.

These capabilities aim to reduce repetitive administrative work and allow database teams to focus on strategic activities.

General availability is planned for Q4 2026.

6. SAP-RPT AI Models: Smarter Predictions and Business Decisions

SAP is expanding its SAP-RPT family of AI models to improve the way AI understands and works with structured enterprise data.

Unlike traditional large language models, which primarily focus on unstructured information, tabular AI is designed to understand structured business data and support more accurate predictions.

Three important developments were announced:

  • SAP-RPT-TS: A time-series forecasting model designed for business scenarios such as demand forecasting. Generally available.
  • SAP-RPT-Decisions: A decision intelligence model designed to automate business decisions across workflows. General availability planned for Q4 2026.
  • SAP-RPT-2: An expanded model supporting multi-table processing, anomaly detection and structured data embeddings. General availability planned for Q1 2027.

SAP also announced the deployment of SAP-RPT on HPE Spaceborne Computer-2 aboard the International Space Station, demonstrating the potential of enterprise AI in edge-computing environments.

7. SAP Document AI: Advancing Intelligent Document Processing

SAP is introducing new capabilities in SAP Document AI to make document processing more intelligent and autonomous.

The new SAP-DOC-1 AI model is designed to extract information from different document formats without extensive upfront configuration.

Additional enhancements include:

  • Document splitting for processing complex, multi-page documents.
  • Custom prompting to define specific information extraction requirements.
  • Deeper integration with Joule Work.
  • Joule Studio capabilities for building document-aware agents and workflows.

These developments will help businesses automate document-intensive processes and reduce manual intervention.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

8. SAP Integration Suite: Stronger Connectivity and AI-Driven Integration

As enterprises adopt more AI agents, seamless connectivity between applications and systems becomes increasingly important.

SAP Integration Suite is receiving several enhancements to support modern integration requirements.

Key announcements include:

  • AI-assisted message processing error resolution.
  • AI-based detection of unusual API request payload sizes.
  • Enhanced GitHub integration for managing integration artifacts.
  • Native RosettaNet support for B2B and supply chain integration.
  • New third-party application adapters for Gmail, Google Sheets, GoToWebinar, Microsoft Excel and Salesforce Service Cloud.
  • Improved monitoring through SAP Cloud ALM.

These enhancements will help organizations simplify integration development, improve operational visibility and prepare their enterprise landscapes for agentic AI.

9. SAP Cloud ERP and RISE with SAP: AI-Driven Transformation

SAP is also evolving the RISE with SAP methodology to help customers adopt AI more effectively as part of their business transformation journeys.

The upcoming enhancements include:

  • AI-enriched implementation guidance and best practices.
  • Personalized onboarding across SAP Autonomous Suite.
  • AI readiness assessments that connect business priorities with relevant AI use cases.
  • Structured transformation road maps to help organizations measure business value.

The focus is on helping customers move beyond technology implementation and achieve measurable business outcomes through AI adoption.

General availability is planned for Q1 2027.

10. New SAP Certifications and Learning Opportunities

Alongside its technology announcements, SAP is investing in building the skills required for the next generation of enterprise AI professionals.

Two important learning developments include:

SAP Business AI Platform Solution Architect Certification

A new certification designed for developers, consultants, partners and solution architects.

It validates expertise across three major platform pillars:

  • Build.
  • Contextualize and reason.
  • Govern.

Joule Studio Developer Certification

SAP has also introduced a Joule Studio developer certification focused on building, extending and managing enterprise AI agents.

As part of its introductory offer, the certification is available free of charge through December 31, 2026.

These learning opportunities provide SAP professionals with a chance to strengthen their expertise in enterprise AI and agentic development.

What Does SAP TechEd 2026 Mean for the Future of Enterprise Technology?

The announcements at SAP TechEd 2026 highlight a significant evolution in the enterprise software landscape.

SAP is moving toward an ecosystem where AI is not simply an assistant that answers questions but an intelligent capability that understands business context, collaborates with other agents and helps execute business processes.

A few major trends stand out:

  1. From generative AI to agentic AI: AI agents are becoming more capable of planning and executing complex workflows.
  2. From disconnected systems to connected intelligence: SAP is strengthening interoperability across SAP and third-party applications.
  3. From generic AI to business-aware AI: SAP Knowledge Graph and Business Data Cloud provide the context needed for enterprise-specific intelligence.
  4. From AI experimentation to enterprise governance: Security, compliance, monitoring and controlled execution are becoming essential components of AI adoption.
  5. From manual development to intent-based development: Tools such as Joule Studio are making it easier to translate business requirements into AI-powered solutions.

Final Thoughts

SAP TechEd 2026 reinforces SAP's vision of the Autonomous Enterprise, where people, business applications, trusted data and intelligent AI agents work together to simplify operations and accelerate business outcomes.

With innovations across Joule Work, Joule Studio, SAP Business AI Platform, SAP Business Data Cloud, SAP HANA Cloud and SAP Integration Suite, SAP is building the foundation for the next generation of intelligent enterprise solutions.

For SAP customers, developers, consultants and technology professionals, these announcements create exciting opportunities to explore agentic AI, modern enterprise architecture and intelligent automation.

The future of SAP is moving beyond simply running business processes. It is about making those processes more intelligent, connected and autonomous.

entry.title: LGM Knowledge Snippet: How warehousing and transportation interact
entry.content:
In SAP Logistics Management, transportation planning and warehouse execution are two sides of the same medal. A shipment cannot leave without the warehouse having picked and staged the goods - and the warehouse cannot start without transportation planning having done its part first(of course, depending on the process you are in). The two disciplines are deeply intertwined: transportation planning determines the carrier and the departure schedule, warehouse execution makes the goods physically ready, and the two services exchange precise signals at every milestone that matters.

This post walks through those signals - per Shipping Process. For each process: what triggers warehouse start, when the Pickup/Delivery Document (PDD) gets linked, and what happens at Staging Completed when the warehouse processing is completed.

LTL (Less-Than-Truckload)

Warehouse start is triggered as soon as the carrier is determined on the Transportation Request - no carrier confirmation is needed. If consolidation is used, the Consignment consolidation must also be finalized first followed by the carrier determination for the consignment. Once the carrier is determined, the items are ready for warehouse processing and handed over.

At Staging Completed:
If packing into Handling Units was done (which may be enforced by the HU mandatory setting in the processing variant), Staging Completed triggers creation of Package Transportation Requests from the HU structure, which adds the HU level for the TR and consignment(in case of consolidation scenarios, where the consignment is created already).

The PDD is not yet linked when warehouse work begins. At Staging Completed, the system searches for an open PDD matching the carrier, shipping point, and planned departure time and links it to the TR. If no match is found, the TR enters an error state requiring manual resolution (see the dedicated post on TR-PDD linking timing).

Direct LTL

The bar is higher: the carrier must actively confirm the Consignment before the warehouse can start. That confirmation also triggers the creation of the PDD based on the carrier confirmation, which is linked to the TR immediately. This means the warehouse knows the carrier and planned departure from the very first step.

At Staging Completed, if packing was required, Package Transportation Requests are created from the HU structure which also updates the consignment  and PDD items are also updated to package level. Because the PDD already exists, no search is needed - the update is direct.

FTL (Full Truck Load)

The subcontracting document in FTL is a Freight Order, not a Consignment. Once the Freight Order is confirmed by the carrier, the included Transportation Requests are released for warehouse processing and planned PDDs are created. The pattern is otherwise identical to Direct LTL: the PDD is known before the warehouse starts, and Staging Completed updates it to package level if packing was done.

Parcel

Like LTL, warehouse start only requires carrier determination on the TR - no Consignment exists yet. The warehouse picks and packs the goods (packing is always mandatory for Parcel). The pivotal moment is Print Label in the packing work center: this triggers Consignment creation, carrier subcontracting, and PDD creation and assignment - all in one step, before the goods reach the staging area. At Staging Completed, Package Transportation Requests are created from the HU structure and PDD items are updated to package level.

 

No Shipping / Customer Self-Pickup

There is no carrier, no Consignment, and no PDD. The Transportation Request is set to "Ready for Warehouse Processing" immediately on creation - no prerequisite at all. The warehouse picks and stages, and the process ends when Staging Completed is confirmed. Transportation planning receives the signal and closes out its side; no loading or carrier handoff follows.

What Staging Completed Always Does

Regardless of Shipping Process, Staging Completed is a firm boundary. Once confirmed, the HU information is final. If a correction is needed - a repack, a quantity change - staging must be explicitly reversed first. The reversal undoes everything Staging Completed triggered: Package TRs are deleted, PDD items revert to product level, and TR statuses step back. Only then can the warehouse re-work and re-confirm.

This is by design: Staging Completed is meant to be a clean, unambiguous signal that transportation can act on with confidence.

entry.title: Re: How do you control and forecast costs for generative...
entry.content:
Hi @thanoj_y ,

Controlling and forecasting costs for Generative AI workloads on SAP BTP requires a combination of usage monitoring, optimization, and budget management.

Some effective practices include:

  1. Set usage quotas and limits: Define token limits, API request limits, and budget thresholds for each application or team to prevent unexpected consumption.
  2. Choose the right AI model: Use smaller, cost-effective models for simple tasks such as text classification, summarization, and basic Q&A. Reserve larger models for complex reasoning tasks.
  3. Implement prompt optimization and caching: Keep prompts concise, avoid sending unnecessary context, reuse responses for repeated queries, and use caching wherever appropriate.
  4. Monitor usage regularly: Use SAP AI Core, SAP AI Launchpad, and SAP BTP cockpit monitoring capabilities, along with available service usage and billing information, to track consumption and identify cost spikes.
  5. Estimate costs before implementation: Start with a small proof of concept and calculate expected monthly usage based on:
    • Number of users and requests per day
    • Average input and output tokens per request
    • Selected model and its pricing
    • Peak usage and expected growth
    • Additional infrastructure and operational costs
  6. Review and optimize continuously: Compare estimated costs with actual consumption, establish budget alerts, and periodically review model selection and application usage patterns.

My recommendation: Build a cost baseline during the POC itself. Measure average token consumption per business transaction, estimate monthly demand, and include a 20–30% buffer for unexpected usage growth.

The goal should not just be to reduce token consumption, but to achieve the best balance between AI response quality, performance, and overall business value.

entry.title: 如何在 SAP Cloud ERP 中为迁移对象添加字段
entry.content:
在将数据迁移到 SAP S/4HANA Cloud 的过程中，标准迁移对象有时无法完全覆盖企业的个性化需求——例如，某些字段并未默认包含在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 的 XML 或 CSV 模板中。 此时，可以借助 「Model Your Migration」（SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler）应用，手动将所需字段添加到迁移对象中。 本文将以 供应商（Supplier） 对象为例，带您一步步完成操作。

         ⚠️ 注意：本文内容仅适用于使用 「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」 方式的场景。

前提条件

  • 具有访问 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」的权限
  • 已分配所需角色：SAP_BR_ADMINISTRATOR
  • 使用的迁移方式为「通过暂存表迁移数据（Migrate Data Using Staging Tables）」
  • 确认您希望添加的字段已被允许使用（请参阅对应 SAP Note，例如 SAP Note 3019787 中关于 Supplier 的说明）。 本示例中，我们将把字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商迁移对象。
  • 所有支持的迁移对象汇总说明，请参阅 SAP Note 2999428。

操作步骤：以供应商迁移对象为例

目标：将字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP 添加到供应商（Supplier）迁移对象中。

1. 打开 Migration Object Modeler 应用

启动 SAP Fiori 应用「Model Your Migration Objects」，并进入您的迁移项目。

首次打开时，系统会提示：该应用仅支持查看和编辑使用「通过暂存表迁移数据」方式的迁移项目和对象。 如需查看使用「直接从 SAP 系统迁移数据（Migrate Data Directly from SAP system）」方式的对象，请通过「实施活动（Implementation Activities）」应用访问 SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler。

 

2. 找到供应商迁移对象

展开迁移对象节点，查看所有对象列表，然后双击「Supplier（供应商）」将其打开。

 

3. 查看源结构（Source Structures）

双击「Source Structures」。 如果界面上看不到技术名称，请点击 Settings（设置） 并开启技术名称显示。

 

 

4. 切换至编辑模式

将应用切换至 Edit（编辑） 模式，以允许对迁移对象进行修改。

 

5. 添加新字段

选择相关的源结构，点击「Add Field（添加字段）」。 输入新字段的详细信息（例如 ZZ_NEW_FIELD）；系统会将其标记为自定义字段。

在本示例中，我们需要添加字段 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP。

 

 

6. 保存更改

保存您的输入。如有需要，可使用「Full Screen on/off」按钮切换视图。

 

7. 映射新字段（Field Mapping）

双击「Field Mapping」（确认仍处于编辑模式）。 在源结构中搜索您刚添加的字段，以及目标侧的对应字段（如 CONTACTALLOWANCECTRCENBP）。

将源字段拖拽到目标字段上完成映射，或者右键点击并选择「Assign Rule（分配规则）」。

 

 

8. 验证并保存映射

仔细检查映射关系是否正确，然后保存更改。

 

9. 同步结构（Synchronize Structures）

执行结构同步，以使您的更改生效。确认弹出的提示框，然后退出应用。

 

10. 在 SAP S/4HANA Migration Cockpit 中验证

返回「Migrate Your Data – Migration Cockpit」，检查您的迁移项目，查看暂存表状态。

  • 如果表状态显示为 「Adjustment Required」，请选中该表并点击「Adjust Structure」。
  • 如果在 Model Your Migration 应用中已完成同步，状态应直接显示为 「OK」。

 

11. 在模板文件中确认字段

新添加的字段现在将出现在迁移对象对应的 XML 模板文件中，可供数据填充使用。

 

补充说明

  • 重置迁移对象： 如有需要，可将迁移对象重置为 SAP 原始模板版本。注意：此操作会移除所有自定义更改。
  • 更新迁移对象： SAP 会定期更新迁移对象。当系统提示更新时，建议及时更新，以确保与最新版本的兼容性。
  • 收藏夹功能： 可将常用的迁移项目或对象添加至收藏夹，方便快速访问（每类最多支持 10 个）。

参考资料

  • SAP Note 3019787 – 通过 Model Your Migration Objects 扩展供应商迁移对象
  • SAP Note 2999428 – 所有支持的迁移对象汇总说明
  • SAP Help Portal – 相关帮助文档
  • SAP S/4HANA Migration Object Modeler for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition（产品文档）
  • 原文： How to Add a Field to a Migration Object in SAP Cloud ERP – SAP Community （作者：Kirstin）

entry.title: Re: Story Reports: Slow and unstable
entry.content:
Hi,

Slow performance in Story Reports can be caused by several factors, including complex data models, large datasets, multiple joins, and backend processing delays.

Since you're experiencing slowness even with smaller reports, I would suggest checking the following:

  1. Try accessing the same report in an incognito window or another supported browser to rule out browser-related issues.
  2.  Review the report's data source, filters, and joins to identify potential performance bottlenecks.
  3.  Check whether the issue occurs for all users or only specific users.
  4. For the saving issue, verify whether the changes persist after reopening the report and check for any error messages. 

If the issue persists across multiple reports and users, I would recommend raising an SAP Support incident with the affected report details, timestamps, and browser console logs.

Also, are you experiencing these issues only while editing Story Reports, or during report execution as well? This would help narrow down the root cause

Thanks,

entry.title: Finding Your Joule Work Desktop Admin URL via SAP for Me
entry.content:
Finding Your Joule Work Desktop Admin URL in SAP for Me

When setting up or troubleshooting Joule Work Desktop, you need the Admin URL. Rather than relying on a bookmarked link — which can become outdated as tenants are updated or migrated — the always-current source of truth is SAP for Me. Here's how to find it.

Why Not Just Bookmark the URL?

The Joule Work Desktop Admin URL can change over time — for example after tenant migrations, infrastructure updates, or re-provisioning. A saved link may silently stop working. Going back to SAP for Me ensures you always get the current, valid URL for your landscape.

Step-by-Step: Find the Current URL in SAP for Me

  1. Open SAP for Me and navigate to Portfolio & Products in the left sidebar.
  2. Click the My Product Packages tab. Depending on your screen width, it may be visible directly in the tab bar or accessible via the More dropdown on the right.
  3. In the left panel, click Customer Landscape — this takes you directly to your landscape without having to open an individual Category first.
  4. Find and expand the formation you used for your Core Components activation (Formation Type: Integration with Joule Core). The formation name typically starts with sap-joule-core but may vary depending on how it was set up in your landscape.
  5. In the Systems table, locate the row with System Type Joule Work Desktop.
  6. The URL column contains your current Admin URL — click the external link icon to open it directly.

The Joule Work Desktop URL found under the sap-joule-core formation in Customer Landscape.

Building and Deploying AI-Powered Applications on SAP BTP Using Claude Code

A Practical Exploration of SAP AI Core, BTP Destinations, Prompt Engineering and Cloud Foundry Deployment

Introduction

Generative AI is changing how developers approach application development. From building intelligent assistants to integrating Large Language Models (LLMs) into enterprise applications, the possibilities are expanding rapidly.

Within the SAP ecosystem, SAP Business Technology Platform (SAP BTP) provides capabilities to build, integrate and deploy enterprise-grade AI-powered applications.

Recently, I explored how Claude Code can be used as part of an AI application development workflow on SAP BTP. During this exploration, I documented the configuration steps, important concepts and deployment process in a practical technical reference.

In this blog, I'd like to share some of the key concepts and learnings from that journey.

 

 

1. Understanding SAP AI Core

SAP AI Core provides a managed environment for integrating AI capabilities into enterprise applications.

It allows applications to interact with supported Large Language Models and provides an enterprise-oriented approach to authentication and connectivity.

Some important concepts include:

  • LLM inference

  • Embeddings

  • Model deployment

  • AI orchestration

The key takeaway is understanding how an application communicates with an AI model through SAP AI Core rather than embedding credentials directly into application code.

2. Understanding the SAP BTP Destination Service

One of the important aspects of enterprise application development is secure connectivity.

SAP BTP Destinations provide centrally managed connection configurations that applications can reference instead of hardcoding connection details.

During my exploration, I focused on:

  • Creating an AI Core service instance.

  • Generating and understanding service keys.

  • Configuring OAuth2 Client Credentials.

  • Mapping service key fields to destination properties.

  • Understanding the difference between application identity and user identity.

A good understanding of destinations makes application connectivity easier to manage and maintain.

3. Prompt Engineering: Defining How Your AI Application Behaves

A model's response depends not only on the model itself but also on how instructions and context are defined.

System prompts help establish the application's role, responsibilities, boundaries and response behavior.

For example, an SAP Procurement Assistant can be instructed to:

  • Retrieve information using available tools.

  • Avoid inventing purchase order or vendor information.

  • Clearly communicate when information is unavailable.

  • Follow defined business and security rules.

The objective is to make AI applications more predictable, consistent and aligned with enterprise requirements.

 

4. From Development to Deployment Using Cloud Foundry

Building an application is only one part of the journey. Making it available in a BTP environment requires proper deployment configuration.

I explored the following concepts:

  • Cloud Foundry API endpoint configuration.

  • SSO-based CLI login.

  • Organization and Space selection.

  • manifest.yml configuration.

  • Service bindings and environment variables.

  • Application deployment using cf push.

Understanding these components helps connect application development with the deployment lifecycle.

5. Exploring MCP and Joule Integration

Another interesting area is connecting AI applications with external tools and enterprise workflows.

The Model Context Protocol (MCP) provides a standardized approach for exposing tools and context to compatible AI clients.

My exploration also included the concept of connecting a deployed application with Joule Work Desktop through its connector configuration.

This opens up interesting possibilities for connecting AI assistants with enterprise capabilities.

6. Key Learnings

A few important takeaways from this exercise:

  1. Secure credential management should be considered from the beginning.

  2. BTP Destinations help separate connectivity configuration from application code.

  3. Well-defined system prompts are essential for predictable AI behavior.

  4. Deployment configuration is as important as application development.

  5. AI integration becomes more useful when combined with enterprise context and tools.

Conclusion

This exploration helped me connect several important concepts across SAP BTP, AI Core, prompt engineering and application deployment.

I have also prepared a practical technical reference covering the configuration steps, examples and deployment checklist to make these concepts easier to revisit.

I hope these learnings are useful to SAP developers, architects and technology enthusiasts who are exploring AI-powered application development.

What are your experiences with Claude Code, SAP AI Core and MCP-based integrations? I'd love to hear your thoughts!

entry.title: Not Every Extra Hour Is Overtime!
entry.content:
Introduction

One of the most common questions in time management is deceptively simple: when does an extra hour become overtime? For full-time employees, the answer is usually clear. For part-time employees, however, an additional hour may first need to bridge the gap to full-time working hours before any overtime premium applies. Getting this distinction right is critical for both compliance and payroll accuracy.

In many company policies (and in some labour laws), a part-timer who works beyond the planned hours is first paid the normal hourly rate until they reach the full-time daily hours. Only the hours after that are real overtime with a premium. And then night hours, days off and public holidays come with their own, higher premium.

I like to think of it like a mobile data plan. Your daily pack is your planned hours. Once it is used up, you can top up at the normal price till you hit the full limit, which is the full-time equivalent. Anything beyond that is charged at the premium rate, and the rate is even higher at night or on a holiday.

In this blog I will share how I built this in SAP SuccessFactors Time Tracking using a few layered time valuations, so that one Time Recording Profile serves both full-timers and part-timers.

Before We Start

  • You already know the basics of Time Tracking: time types, time type groups, time valuations, time recording profiles and business rules for time valuation.
  • Employees record clock times (clock in and clock out), so that segment filters can find night hours.
  • Extra hours are recorded with a separate overtime time type and approved by the manager.
  • Example rates used: 50% premium for weekday day overtime, 100% for night overtime (22:00 to 06:00) and for every hour on days off and public holidays, plus a 20% night allowance. Kindly adjust to your policy.
  • The names used here are generic. Please rename them as per your own naming convention.

The Big Picture: An Overtime Ladder

Every recorded hour has to answer three simple questions, in this order:

  1. Is it within my planned hours? Then it is normal paid time.
  2. Is it within the full-time daily hours? Then it is Overtime Regular, paid at the normal hourly rate.
  3. Is it beyond the full-time hours? Then it is real overtime: 50% on a working day, 100% at night or on a day off or public holiday.

In the system, this becomes five small layers. Each layer does only one job and passes the rest down, like water flowing through a set of filters.

 

The overtime ladder: two lines, one subtraction and then the premium sorting.

Building the Layers, Step by Step

Here are the ten valuations at a glance.

#

Layer

What to configure

Output

1

Gatekeeper

Filter Single Records from Input Groups on registered overtime, approved records only. Add an error check if hours above the plan are not recorded as overtime.

Approved Overtime

2

Full-time ruler

Calculation by Business Rule, per day, input = planned working time. Return 8 hours (or 7 for a reduced norm), and 0 on days off and public holidays.

Full-Time Daily Threshold

3

Line A: part-time

Aggregate Input Groups and Split, per day. Input = recorded time + approved overtime. Threshold = planned working time group.

Below: Within Planned; Above: Above Planned

4

Line B: full-time

Same split on the same input. Threshold = Full-Time Daily Threshold.

Below: Within Full-Time; Above: Overtime Base

5

Normal-rate top-up

Aggregate and Split. Input = Within Full-Time + Within Planned (Reverse Sign = Yes). Fixed threshold 0.

Overtime Regular (factor 1)

6

Day or night

Filter Segments from Input Groups on Overtime Base, segment 06:00 to 22:00.

Inside: Overtime Day; Outside: Overtime Night

7

Calendar check

Filter Input Groups on Overtime Day, Time Records Filter = days off and public holidays.

Match: Overtime Non-Working Day; Rest: Overtime 50% Premium

8

100% bucket

Aggregate Overtime Night + Overtime Non-Working Day, fixed threshold 0.

Overtime 100% Premium

9

Night allowance

Filter Segments on recorded time + approved overtime, segment 06:00 to 22:00.

Outside: Night Allowance 20%

10

Profile

Assign all valuations to the clock-time Time Recording Profile in this same order.

One profile for FT and PT

A few tips that saved me some headache:

  • Days off and public holidays are entirely overtime. Because the full-time rule returns 0 on these days, every hour jumps straight over both lines into Overtime Base. No Overtime Regular is created, and the calendar check in step 7 sends it all to the 100% bucket.
  • Keep pay types only on the final buckets. Overtime Regular, Overtime 50% Premium, Overtime 100% Premium and Night Allowance 20% go to payroll (automatic payout after the bookable period of TOIL). Everything in between is just a working group.
  • Order matters. A valuation can only read a group that an earlier valuation has already filled.

Let Us See It in Action

Three employees, three different days. Watch where each hour lands.

 

Group

Part-timer, weekday

Full-timer, weekday

Part-timer, Sunday

The same part-timer earns the normal rate on a weekday up to 8 hours, but on a Sunday every single hour is premium. Same person, same profile, different answer, exactly as the policy wants.

Watch Out For These

  • It is daily, not periodic. Everything is valuated per day against the daily planned hours. It does not look at weekly averages or the settlement period. If your overtime is decided at the end of a settlement period, you need period-based valuations or payroll logic on top.
  • The calendar must be right. Days off come from the work schedule and holidays from the holiday calendar. If either is wrong, the hours fall into the wrong bucket.
  • Hours fill from morning to night. The split fills the earliest hours first, so evening hours become overtime.
  • Night overtime is paid twice by design. It gets the 100% premium and the night allowance.

Wrapping Up

Part-time overtime is rarely a single calculation. Each hour needs to be classified, evaluated, and routed correctly before the right payment outcome can be reached.

That is why a layered valuation design works so well. One valuation identifies additional hours, another measures them against full-time thresholds, and a third applies the appropriate premium. Each layer has a single responsibility, making the overall solution easier to understand and maintain.

Have you tackled this challenge differently in SuccessFactors Time Tracking? Share your approach in the comments. The best ideas in our community usually come from comparing solutions.

entry.title: Multiple adresses for a single customer
entry.content:
Hello,

I would like to understand how we can manage multiple addresses using the multiple address handling functionality in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition. Specifically, I would appreciate your guidance on the following:

  1. How can we create a single customer code with multiple addresses?

  2. How can we maintain different addresses against the same customer code?

  3. How can we use these different addresses as Ship-to Parties in sales orders?

Any documentation would also be helpful.

entry.title: Re: Multiple adresses for a single customer
entry.content:
Hello

Prerequisites

Before using any of the three capabilities below, activate two configuration switches in the Configure Your Solution app (search: "Address handling"). Activate them in this order:

  1. Activate Multiple Address Handling for Customer Master Data in SAP BP (ID: 105612): enables address-dependent data in customer master records.
  2. Activate Multiple Address Handling in SD Documents Using SAP BP: enables SD documents to consume the multiple addresses.

These switches are irreversible. Once set to ON, they cannot be reversed. Reference: KBA 3776974 — How to activate Multiple Address Handling

1. How to Create a Single Customer Code with Multiple Addresses
The SAP Business Partner (BP) data model natively supports multiple addresses per BP record. One customer number can represent a legal entity with as many physical addresses as needed.

  1. Open app Manage Customer Master Data (ID: F0850A) or Manage Business Partner Master Data.
  2. Search for the customer record and open it in Edit mode.
  3. Go to the Address Overview tab.
  4. Choose Create to add a new address.
  5. Enter address details (country, city, street, postal code).
  6. Set a validity period (Valid From / Valid To).
  7. Assign an Address Usage (for example: Delivery Address / SHIP_TO).
  8. Save.

Reference: SAP Help — Multiple Address Handling in SD Documents Using SAP Business Partner

2. How to Maintain Different Addresses Against the Same Customer Code

After the configuration switches are active, each additional address in the BP record can carry its own:

  • Validity period:time-dependent addresses, the system checks validity automatically during document processing.
  • Address-dependent data: sales area-specific fields (such as incoterms, delivery terms, tax classification) can differ per address within the same customer number. This data propagates automatically to the sales document when the corresponding address is selected.
  • Address Usage: classifies the address role (for example: standard, delivery, billing). If more than one address shares the same usage type, one must be set as the standard.

This replaces the older approach of creating a separate customer master record for each physical location.

Reference: SAP Help — Business Partner Address Definition

3. How to Use These Addresses as Ship-to Parties in Sales Orders
When multiple address handling is active, the system integrates the BP addresses directly into partner determination in SD documents. Behavior during sales order creation:

  • After entering the Sold-to Party, the system automatically proposes suitable addresses for partner functions (sold-to party, ship-to party, bill-to party) based on the addresses and their usages maintained in the BP master.
  • In the Partners tab of the sales order header (or item), an address selection button is available for each partner function.
  • The user can click the button and select any valid BP address for the Ship-to Party.
  • If address-dependent data exists for the selected address, the system copies it automatically into the sales document.

Important constraint: The Payer partner function supports only the standard address. Multiple address selection is not available for the payer.

References:

  • KBA 3633898 — Cannot select multiple address for payer
  • SAP Help — Multiple Customer Addresses and Address-Dependent Data
  • SAP Help — Understanding Address Selection in SD Documents

entry.title: Re: How to Retrieve Processing Results for Asynchronous S...
entry.content:
For asynchronous Journal Entry APIs, SAP provides corresponding outbound confirmation services to return the final business processing result to the sending system.

For example, the Journal Entry – Clearing (Asynchronous) API uses:

Inbound service: JournalEntryBulkClearingRequest_In

Outbound service: JournalEntryBulkClearingConfirmation_Out

Communication scenario: SAP_COM_0002

To receive the outbound confirmation:

Populate SenderBusinessSystemID in the inbound SOAP request.

Ensure the sender business system is correctly associated with the relevant Communication System and Communication Arrangement.

Configure a receiving SOAP endpoint, for example using SAP Integration Suite (Cloud Integration), to accept the outbound confirmation.

SAP S/4HANA Cloud uses the sender business system information to determine the recipient of the confirmation. If the required routing information is missing or incorrectly configured, the outbound confirmation cannot be delivered.

The confirmation provides the business processing result, including accounting document details, company code, fiscal year and relevant log information. Reference information can be used to correlate the confirmation with the original request.

Error Handling

Errors occurring at the SOAP framework or AIF processing level may not generate an outbound confirmation because they occur outside the specific Journal Entry API processing logic.

Such errors should be investigated using the Message Dashboard/AIF monitoring functionality in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition.

Note: This outbound confirmation pattern applies to asynchronous Journal Entry APIs that provide corresponding confirmation services. The applicable confirmation and error-handling mechanisms should be verified in the documentation of each individual API.

Errors in warehouse distribution are now surfaced on the freight document with a targeted resolution action. Status tracking for execution events from carriers and logistics partners — pick-up confirmations, delivery notifications, delay alerts — is now fully visible on the freight document, so any issue is immediately apparent and actionable by the team responsible. These improvements reduce the time from exception to resolution, protect customer commitments, and lower the operational cost of exception management.

This release adds further configurable controls over who can lift compliance blocks on freight documents. For companies moving dangerous goods or managing trade compliance obligations, restricting this authority to designated approvers — without requiring custom development — reduces regulatory risk and provides a cleaner audit trail.

 

Sustainability Reporting: Actual Carrier Emissions, Automatically

Regulatory pressure on emissions reporting is increasing. Collecting accurate emissions data from carriers has historically been a manual, fragmented, and resource-intensive process. This release integrates carrier-reported greenhouse gas emissions directly into the freight transaction, at both the shipment and individual route-leg level — eliminating manual data collection and reducing reliance on estimates. The result is higher-quality emissions data for disclosure purposes and less operational effort to produce sustainability reports. For a detailed look at how carrier emissions data flows into TM, see the [GHG Emissions blog on SAP Community].

 

Lower Total Cost of Ownership, Simpler Upgrades

Custom code is one of the most persistent sources of cost and complexity in enterprise logistics platforms. It inflates implementation budgets, creates risk at upgrade time, and requires ongoing maintenance as the business evolves. This release addresses that challenge directly. A new generation of standard, extensible interfaces for the core TM documents are now available, designed to accommodate customer-specific integration requirements without the overhead of custom code. The result is a lower total cost of ownership, faster and less disruptive upgrade cycles, and a more sustainable path for evolving the platform alongside the business.

entry.title: Agent Skills for SAP Commerce Cloud, Composable Storefront: teaching AI agents the right patterns
entry.content:
AI coding agents have quietly become part of how storefronts get built. Developers reach for them to scaffold a component, wire up a service, or make sense of an unfamiliar codebase, and they expect the framework underneath to cooperate when they do.

For a framework such as Composable Storefront (Spartacus), working well with AI coding agents is becoming as much a part of the developer experience as solid documentation once was. In the October release of Composable Storefront (221121.20), we're taking a deliberate step to meet that expectation: adopting Agent Skills, an open standard for teaching AI coding tools how to write correct Composable Storefront code. It's one piece of a broader investment in making SAP Commerce Cloud work well with AI tooling.

The gap

Here's the problem we set out to solve. Ask an AI coding agent to build a Composable Storefront feature today, for example a product-comparison component, and it will usually hand you something that compiles and runs. Look closer, though, and it has written generic Angular: it injects HttpClient straight into the component, builds the API URL by hand, and parses the response inline. The code works in isolation, but it doesn't follow the Composable Storefront architecture conventions.
 
The reason is straightforward. Generic Angular is everywhere in the training data these models learned from; Composable Storefront's own architecture is more thinly represented. So when a coding agent reaches for a pattern, it reaches for the generic Angular one it has seen countless times rather than the Composable Storefront one. That output isn't wrong Angular, it just isn't how Composable Storefront is built. The Composable Storefront framework is deliberately opinionated: data flows through a facade, then a connector, an adapter, and a normalizer; components are placed on a page by the CMS rather than by an Angular route; URLs, translations, and configuration each run through their own layers. Code that skips these conventions compiles fine but will eventually land as rework on whoever has to fit it back into the Composable Storefront conventions later.

There's a compounding effect, too: coding agents read the surrounding codebase and imitate what they find, so an early misguided pattern shortcut tends to multiply. It can run the other way as well: even Angular's own AI tooling sometimes suggests newer patterns that Composable Storefront hasn't adopted yet.

What we shipped

So we taught the tools. The October release ships a single Agent Skill (spartacus-developer, published as the @Spartacus/skills package) that captures how Composable Storefront code should actually be written. It covers 16 patterns, grouped across the framework:

Backend and state

  • Backend communication through the facade, connector, adapter, and normalizer pipeline
  • Using facades instead of reaching into the NgRx store
  • Extending backend data with normalizers
  • State management with NgRx or Commands and Queries

Pages, routing, and CMS

  • CMS component wiring and placement
  • Outlets for adding UI into existing pages
  • Routing and configurable URLs
  • CMS-driven lazy loading

Components, styling, and rendering

  • RxJS subscriptions and change detection
  • Styling
  • Internationalization
  • Server-side-rendering safety

Configuration and reuse

  • Configuration
  • Correct injector placement
  • Reusing framework features that already exist
  • Extending framework classes rather than replacing them

A few things make Agent Skills the right vehicle for this:

  • They load only what's relevant. A skill uses progressive disclosure: a short, always-visible description tells the coding agent when the skill applies, and the detailed guidance for a given pattern loads only when a matching task comes up. That lets the skill carry real depth (full pipeline walkthroughs, the rules for each layer) without weighing down every unrelated prompt.
  • They work across the tools developers already use. Agent Skills are an open standard adopted across Anthropic, OpenAI, Cursor, Microsoft, and others so the same guidance serves the most popular coding harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, OpenCode, and others. It isn't a bet on a single vendor.
  • They activate on their own. The coding agent recognizes Composable Storefront work and pulls in the skill without the developer having to name it.
Alongside the pattern guidance, the skill carries a set of NEVER/ALWAYS lines that catch the most common mistakes, and it bundles copy-paste debugging recipes that surface runtime state which is otherwise hard to see, such as the resolved OCC endpoints or the current CMS page structure. So it helps with existing storefronts as well as newly generated code. It's worth being clear about scope: the skill focuses on writing correct code. Adjacent tasks like upgrades or migrating an Accelerator storefront to Composable Storefront are separate challenges we're addressing through other initiatives.

Measuring the effectiveness

Before shipping, we wanted evidence the skill actually helps, so we built a way to measure it. An evaluation harness generates two identical Composable Storefront app templates that differ only in whether the skill is present, runs the same realistic tasks against both, and scores the output with an independent AI judge, one that never sees which version produced which code and marks against the skill's own rules. Our evaluation protocol requires each tested model's average adherence score to meet or exceed its no-skill baseline.
 
The initial results are encouraging: across the patterns we track, the skill cut architectural deviations by roughly half. Both a smaller, cheaper model and a larger, stronger one improved; the smaller one most, which makes sense, since the stronger model already infers more of the framework on its own. These are initial measurements against a no-skill baseline, with the usual run-to-run variation, so we treat them as a starting point rather than a final verdict. But the direction is clear, and we now have a repeatable way to catch regressions as Composable Storefront, Angular, and the models themselves keep evolving.

Try it today

Getting started follows the standard Composable Storefront setup. When you install or update with the schematics, you're prompted to add the agent skills and choose which AI-tool folders to target:

# New project
ng add @spartacus/schematics

# Existing project
ng update @spartacus/schematics

Select one or both of the .claude/skills/ and .agents/skills/ folders at the prompt, and the schematic installs the package and copies the skill for you; there's nothing to wire up by hand. If you already have a project and just want to add the skill on its own, install @Spartacus/skills (matching your Composable Storefront version) and run ng generate @Spartacus/schematics:ai-context. Either way, your AI coding agent discovers the skill automatically once it's in place.  See our Help Portal documentation page for further details.

What's next

This is a first step. As Composable Storefront, Angular, and the models keep evolving, we'll keep the skill current. We'll also keep investing in how Composable Storefront works with AI coding agents more broadly, and the most useful input we can get is yours. Install the skill, put it to work on real tasks, and tell us where it helps and where it can be improved. That feedback will help us shape where we take this next.
Tried the skill and have thoughts on it? Reach out to steve.sisalith@sap.com.
